newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE Albania envoy says seeks talks on democracy.
newsitem.headline: OSCE Albania envoy says seeks talks on democracy.

text.p: The Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe's (OSCE) special envoy to Albania, Franz Vranitzky, said on Wednesday he would seek talks with the Albanian government on democracy and human rights.

The former Austrian chancellor said on Austria's state radio he wanted to discuss "principles that are valid in Europe -- democracy, political rights, human rights, everything that is a natural part of a functioning democracy".

The OSCE said late on Tuesday it had appointed Vranitzky as its special envoy to Tirana and had asked him to assess the situation in the troubled Balkan nation. Vranitzky is expected to travel to Albania before the end of the week.

Albania has been rocked by a wave of violent unrest sparked by the collapse of high-risk investment funds. The government declared emergency rule and said it was determined to crush the unrest, which has claimed at least 20 lives.
"I want to approach the affair as impartially as possible and use all possibilities that international co-operation can offer," Vranitzky said.
Western countries which backed President Sali Berisha when he came to power in 1992, two years after the collapse of Europe's harshest communist government, have widely criticised the emergency rule.

Asked whether the west had misjudged Berisha, Vranitzky said: "I wouldn't want to say that. He was not only a partner for talks with Austria, but also...with the European Union and particularly with the OSCE."
